summary: @ornikar/apollo-link-timeout preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a small Apollo Link that aborts requests past a timeout, but ships a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases (pinned v1.3.13), extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` against a bundled 727KB single-line Bun-compiled file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is heavily obfuscated (shuffled string/numeric constant array with a rotator-style decoder function) and is not referenced by the package's declared `main` (`lib/timeoutLink.js`) — it exists solely to be executed by the preinstall-fetched Bun runtime. The alternate-runtime layer means the payload's behavior is not visible to Node-based scanners, and the runtime and payload are unrelated to the advertised Apollo timeout functionality. This matches the alternate-runtime-dropper shape: fetching a second language runtime at install time to execute an opaque bundled blob.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
